title: The composition of a domain graph
description:
What a domain graph is made of, and where each part is decided. A node file says what one kind is; this file says what has to exist besides the eight of them before a graph can be composed at all.

The graph itself is derived and never authored: its nodes are the authored files and its edges are the relationships those files declare in their own frontmatter. A relationship stated only in prose is not an edge, because two readings of one paragraph produce two graphs.

nodes.what: One file per kind, eight of them, each declaring what its kind requires of its own content.

envelope.what: The fields every node carries whatever its kind, and which of them the enrichment owns.

identifiers.what: Every identifier pattern, and the arithmetic between an identifier and its path. A pattern spells the kinds, so it belongs to the profile and cannot be shared across profiles.
identifiers.status: authored here; today inside the monolith's $defs

primitives.what: The twelve attribute types and the parameters each requires and does not inherit.
primitives.status: authored here; today inside the monolith's $defs

vocabularies.what: Every closed enumeration: the kinds, the ddd sets per kind, origin, gap kind, subdomain type, ownership, context-relationship pattern, binding — and the two fields that are rejected rather than absent.
vocabularies.status: authored here; today scattered across the monolith's properties

edges.what: The closed edge vocabulary with cardinality, traversal and depth. It is what makes a reference resolvable and what a validator enforces.
edges.status: authored here; had no machine-readable home — prose in the specification, a hand transcription in bin/materialize.py, and no comparison between them

body_sections.what: The two headings each kind names, and the form a body takes.
body_sections.status: authored here; had no machine-readable home

invariants.what: The cross-kind conditionals, and the rules that need to see more than one node.
invariants.status: authored here; the cross-kind half is inside the monolith's allOf, the cross-node half is inside bin/check_knowledge.py

system_defaults.what: The timezone, currency and identity strategy every attribute inherits, plus the body-line ceiling. Facts about the repository that installs the framework, never shipped defaults.

materialized_graph.what: The derived form: nodes, edges, and the edge vocabulary carried with them so a consumer reads the traversal policy from the artifact rather than from whatever materialized it.
materialized_graph.status: exists; its node-kind enum disagrees with the eight kinds, so a graph derived from a real base fails it

projections.what: The three views the ontology admits — an index, a glossary, a context map. Reproducible from the graph and never a normative source.
projections.status: exists; no schema, because a projection is read and never parsed for a decision

x-graph.nodes_are: the authored files, one per construct
x-graph.edges_are: the relationships those files declare, per domain/tables/edges.json
x-graph.never: authored, hand-edited, or inferred from prose

x-composes-into.why: The shipped contract is loaded standalone by a consumer's validator, which would resolve a cross-file $ref over the network. So the distribution carries one self-contained file and this tree is what it is composed from — the same arrangement schemas/knowledge-notation.json and schemas/contract-versions.json already use.
x-composes-into.not_yet: The composition step does not exist. Until it does, this tree and the shipped contract are two homes for one set of facts, and the shipped one is the authority.
x-composes-into.version_effect: Composing this tree carries three breaking changes into the frontmatter contract: `knowledgeObjectId` becomes `nodeId`, `steps[].ko` becomes `steps[].node`, and `governed_by` is removed. Each requires a contract version bump and a migration.
